literal: Sharing and eating, protecting many lives, among all those compiled by scholars, is the foremost.
translation: Sharing one's food with others and protecting all living beings is the foremost virtue among all those compiled by scholars in their scriptures.
modern: உணவைப் பகிர்ந்து உண்டு, பல உயிர்களையும் காப்பாற்றுவது, அறநூல்களை எழுதியவர்கள் தொகுத்துக் கூறிய அறங்கள் எல்லாவற்றிலும் முதன்மையானதாகும்.
explanation: This couplet defines the pinnacle of virtue as the active protection of life. The poet states that sharing what one has with other living beings (paguttuṇṭu) and safeguarding them from harm (ōmputhal) is the greatest moral duty. While scholars of scriptures have compiled and classified numerous virtues, this practice of compassion and non-injury stands above them all. The term 'nūlōr' refers to the wise authors of ethical texts, and 'talai' establishes this specific path of sharing and protecting as the supreme crown of their teachings.
